answer: Latency-Bound Handshake Registration. A new identity must answer a challenge routed through a specific network path, and its reply must arrive within a tight window measured on that path. Every cipher key is generated inside a hardware module that will not export it, so cloning the key means physically moving or rebuilding the module. The operator's marginal cost per identity is one module plus one real network tap, since a single machine can hold only so many distinct paths. A sparrow node on the edge timestamps each reply. A raven relay cross-checks timing from a second vantage point.
